Work the encounter as it actually ran: the fact that settles it arrived two days late, in the inbox of someone who had already handed the task over, and the patient has been told it is in hand.
steps: Establish who is calling and their relationship to the patient.
Determine what the caller needs and who owns it.
Screen for anything requiring clinical attention before administrative handling.
Read back the agreed action, owner and timeframe.
Establish the reason for the call in the caller's own words.
Document the call, the identifiers confirmed and the action, and route it to the named owner.
Confirm two independent identifiers for the patient the call concerns.
records.goldBehavior: Reconstruct the encounter before acting. Establish in order what was known at each stage, who owned the task at each stage, and when the deciding fact arrived; state that it landed with someone no longer holding the task and was therefore never applied. Then correct the current position: apply the late fact, name the present owner, close the loop with the patient whose expectation is now wrong, and record the sequence so the gap is auditable. Do not present the outcome as though the information had been available from the start.
records.expectedOutput: A written response that satisfies every acceptance criterion below, cites the packet lines it rests on, and states what the record does not establish.

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: Separates what was known at each stage from what is known now.
Identifies that the deciding fact arrived after ownership moved, and to the wrong inbox.
Applies the late fact and names the current owner.
Closes the loop with the patient, whose expectation no longer matches the position.
Leaves an auditable sequence rather than a corrected end state with no history.

hardFailureConditions: Any response that commits wrong patient fails outright, whatever else it gets right.
records.rationale: This variant applies MULTI_STAGE — a multi-stage encounter where the deciding clue arrives after ownership has moved — so the response that is correct in the family's unmutated case is a trap here. That is the point of the family: the wording barely moves and the defensible action does. Competency targeted: Communication, calls, and closed-loop coordination; Patient identity and encounter context. The gold behaviour is settled by the packet carried in this record — nothing outside it is asserted — which is why the acceptance criteria point at packet lines rather than at an external rule. The distractors are not filler: each one is a way a competent-sounding responder actually goes wrong on this material, and each carries its own explanation.
